outline_comparison: Same skeleton, minus Begg's long Acts 16-18 travelogue. From the moment the FBC preacher reaches 'here we move into chapter 1, verse one' [00:43:48] to the final 'Amen' [01:18:35], the sequence of ideas is Begg's, point for point and in Begg's order: Paul-means-little (Chrysostom, Thecla, Eph 3:8, Isa 66:2) -> Silas/Sylvanus/Pennsylvania and Timothy -> ekklesia and 'no buildings' -> Father and Son plus the Spirit -> grace and peace, Saul of Tarsus, fountain-and-stream, the junkie -> the three causes of thankfulness in Begg's headings ('the work which springs from faith', 'the labor prompted by love', 'the endurance inspired by hope') -> the closing triad 'a faith that functions, a love that labors, a hope that endures/hangs on' -> a closing prayer that follows Begg's prayer clause by clause. The FBC preacher drops Begg's 25-minute Acts background section and substitutes a Barna worldview-survey opener, and he inserts his own illustrations at Begg's illustration slots. Where Begg's structure changes, the FBC sermon changes with it.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher replaces Begg's entire 25-minute Acts 16-18 historical background with a contemporary-research opener, and he substitutes his own illustrations at most of Begg's illustration slots while keeping Begg's exegetical skeleton, headings, phrasing and closing prayer. The original content is almost entirely (a) the Barna worldview-survey introduction, (b) sports/pop-culture illustrations, (c) local and personal references, and (d) heavy call-and-response interaction with the room. Almost none of the original material is exegetical: where the sermon explains the text, it is Begg's explanation.

personalisation_patterns: British details Americanised: Begg's 'I bring my wife a cup of tea in the morning' becomes 'I brought my spouse a cup of coffee in the morning' (1:07:17).
Begg's own church name swapped for the local one: 'they may think of Parkside Church' becomes 'When others think of you and us as a church... when they think of the people at FBC' (1:16:56).
Begg's unnamed authority kept unnamed but warmed up: 'One of the commentators says' becomes 'I I love this comment. A commentator said this very helpfully' (1:00:41).

Begg's self-deprecating aside about his own surname ('the name Begg means little... a Gallic name') is dropped and replaced with the preacher's own name story: 'my mother gave me a name when I was four years old and called me the world king' (0:45:59).

Begg's declarative sentences converted into call-and-response for a participatory room: 'for there was no building into which to go' becomes 'You know why? There were no buildings' (0:53:17); 'he who is humble and contrite in spirit' becomes 'Let's say that together' (0:46:48).

Begg's dated cultural markers refreshed: Begg's materialist climbing a ladder propped against the wrong wall is dropped for pornography addiction; Begg's 'late 20th century' Cleveland framing is replaced by 2026 Barna data and the Strait of Hormuz.

Begg's illustration slots preserved but refilled: at the 'labor/burning' slot Begg's 'burned out for the cause of Jesus Christ' triggers a Spurgeon quotation of the FBC preacher's own; at the endurance slot Begg's Barclay/George Matheson quotation is replaced by the Harbaugh family story.

Superlatives added to Begg's restrained phrasing: 'a love that cost God his son' becomes 'the love that costs God his only son'; 'we're rightly jealous of this church' becomes 'how proper it is to be rightly envious of this church'.
rating_rationale: From verse 1 onward this sermon is Begg's sermon on the same text, re-delivered: the exegetical points, their order, their headings, and most of the connective prose track 'Faith, Hope and Love' clause by clause, and the machine alignment finds 23 overlapping regions covering roughly 18% of the sermon window even before accounting for looser paraphrase. The borrowings are of the strongest kind — an unattributed commentator quote, an apocryphal description of Paul, a four-step etymological digression about Pennsylvania, two paired 'labor of love' vignettes, the 'shrug is the answer' peroration, the closing 'faith that functions / love that labors / hope that endures' tagline, and finally a closing prayer prayed back almost clause for clause. Begg is never named, Truth For Life is never named, and no borrowing is signalled in any form; the preacher instead tells the congregation this is material 'that I never heard before I studied it'. It is not a 10 because the delivery is genuinely his own: he discards Begg's entire Acts background section, opens with 2026 Barna research, adds a dozen original illustrations (Harbaugh, Spurgeon, CarShield, the sandwich technique, the world-king story), and reworks the whole thing into a call-and-response style utterly unlike Begg's. But the sermon's spine, its scholarship and its prayer are borrowed wholesale.

caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captions and the Begg text is Whisper ASR; both mangle proper nouns identically in places (Chrysostom -> 'Christom'/'Chrysostom', Thecla -> 'Thela'/'Fechler', Sylvanus -> 'Sylvanius'/'Sovenas'), so exact-word identity scores understate the real overlap and occasional odd wording ('his Roman improper name', 'a second century doctrine') is likely a transcription error rather than the preacher's.

Alignment regions 1, 2, 3, 8 and 14 are Scripture (1 Thess 1:1-5, Isaiah 66:2, John 14:27) being read or quoted by both men and are NOT evidence of borrowing; region 5 is flagged 'likely_scripture Ezekiel' by the heuristic but is actually the apocryphal Acts of Paul and Thecla description, which IS strong evidence.

Some overlapping phrases are stock evangelical or standard reference-work material and carry little weight on their own: 'grace and peace', the ekklesia/Athens-assembly gloss, 1 Peter 2:9 'out of darkness into his marvelous light', the Watts hymn line 'Love so amazing, so divine', and 'salvation is by faith not works'. The evidence here rests on the sequence and the connective prose around them, not on any single phrase.

The FBC preacher's two congregational assignments (read the letter daily; write someone a letter of appreciation) were given the previous Sunday and are only recapped in this recording, so the borrowing of Begg's two asides is attested here at second hand.

I checked the other 21 Begg transcripts in source_transcripts/ for the FBC-original illustrations (Spurgeon 'watch me burn', Harbaugh, Barna, the sandwich technique, kamikaze pilot, Rembrandt, 'pick of the litter', 'attendance, buildings and cash') and found no matches, so this sermon draws on volume1/01-faithhopelove and no other Begg message in the archive.
